messages:
anya: quick experiment report — trying a memory-aware 'soft-shedding' admission hook to reduce KV-cache OOMs during long-context inference. repro was on latest music-gen job spike around 03:12 UTC, sudden run of 8k token requests caused KV blowups.

anya: sketch of the admission rule i pushed as a feature-flag (flag: runtime.soft_shed_v2):
```
# pseudo-config
admission:
  mode: soft_shed
  kv_util_threshold: 0.78         # fraction of kv memory we treat as high pressure
  token_budget_target: 1024       # preferred max tokens per batch under pressure
  score_weights: {kv_bytes: 0.7, tokens: 0.3}
  min_pass_rate: 0.2              # allow a small fraction through to avoid starvation
```

anya: quick profiler snippet from the run (sampled):
```
queue_depth=18, avg_req_tokens=676, avg_kv_bytes=14.6MB, kv_free=420MB, est_full_usage=0.85
batches_assembled=72, aborted_for_memory=6, partial_shed=11
OOMs=3 (all on batch assembly step)
```

anya: question — does this weighting and min_pass_rate sound reasonable? any quick suggestions before I run a 12h canary?

sam: looks reasonable. two quick concerns: 1) the estimator for kv_bytes needs to be per-slot (model variant + seq len + kv-dtype). we should avoid a single global avg. 2) min_pass_rate should be dynamic based on p99 latency SLO. if we force 20% through under high pressure we could blow latency.

liam: +1 to per-slot estimator. also suggest using an EWMA of kv_util (60s window) so transient spikes don't shed too hard. formula suggestion for score:
```
score = alpha * normalized_kv_est + beta * (req_tokens / token_budget_target)
```
then drop if score > 1.0. alpha/beta tuned by percentile of historical OOM precursors.

jen: if we start shedding, add observability to show what fraction of requests lost signals that matter (e.g., webhooks vs background). we should favor shedding low-priority routes first. also add automatic rollback trigger if error rate for client-visible routes > 0.5%.

anya: good catches. i already scoped per-slot estimator (using model, quant, seq_profile) — left that out of the snippet for brevity. implementing EWMA on kv_util is trivial.

anya: quick canary plan: enable flag on one pool, 4h ramp, traffic split 10% -> 30% if no regressions. monitor: OOMs, p50/p95 latency, token-throttle events, route_error_rate. roll back immediately if OOMs increase or route_error_rate > 0.5%.

sam: please also emit a histogram of "score" and "reason" tags (kv_high / token_high / both) — will help tune alpha/beta.

liam: small perf note — computing per-request kv_estimator is a few hundred microseconds if we do naive iteration. use a cached bucket map keyed by (model, qlevel, seq_bucket) to keep admission fast.

ci-bot: experiment flagged: runtime.soft_shed_v2=true on pool gpu-prod-7, PR: #4125, owner: @anya. Canary window: 2026-03-17T03:30Z -> 2026-03-17T07:30Z. Alerts: infra-oom, perf-regressions.

anya: thanks — i'll add the histograms and the cached estimator. will report back after the 4h ramp. anyone want to be on watch?

jen: i'll take the first two hours, ping me on pager if any OOM alarms. :thumbsup:

sam: i'll look at the score histograms and alpha/beta tuning during the ramp.

liam: can help with the estimator cache if needed.

anya: awesome. landing the canary now. will post a short summary with numbers after the run.
